Section I: Notice Inviting Tender (NIT)
1. Notice Inviting Tender
Department of Digital Learning Infrastructure (DDLI) invites bids for entering into an item-rate contract for supply,
installation, configuration and warranty support of laptop computer sets for government training and administrative
facilities. The tender reference is DDLI/PROC/GOODS/2026-27/014.
Bidders shall read the complete Tender Document before submitting a bid. The Tender Information Summary below
provides salient information but does not replace the detailed clauses.

3. Eligibility Criteria
(cid:127) Bidder shall be a manufacturer of the offered laptops or an authorised dealer/distributor of the OEM.
(cid:127) Bidder shall possess valid PAN and GST registration applicable to the offered business.
(cid:127) Bidder shall not be insolvent, bankrupt, under receivership or wound up.
(cid:127) Bidder shall not be blacklisted, banned or debarred by the procuring organisation or otherwise declared ineligible under
applicable procurement rules.
(cid:127) Bidder shall declare absence of a conflict of interest with other bidders and the procuring organisation.
(cid:127) Where the bidder is an authorised dealer, a tender-specific OEM authorisation letter shall be submitted.
(cid:127) Bidder shall meet the qualification criteria in Section VIII.
4. Bid Security and Performance Security
For this mock tender, a Bid Securing Declaration shall be submitted in Form 7. Performance Security shall be applicable
at 3% of the accepted contract value and shall be furnished in the prescribed form within the period stated in the Letter of
Award.
5. Submission and Opening
Bids shall be uploaded electronically in two covers: Cover 1 – Techno-commercial bid and Cover 2 – Financial bid/BOQ.
The financial bid shall be opened only for bidders whose techno-commercial bid is found responsive and technically
suitable.

Section II: Instructions to Bidders (ITB)
1. Tender Document and Bid Structure
The Tender Document comprises the NIT/TIS, ITB, AITB, GCC, SCC, Schedule of Requirements, Technical
Specifications and Quality Assurance, Qualification Criteria and Bidding Forms. The financial BOQ is an integral part of
the tender.
The reference MTD states that Section VI covers goods, quantities, HSN codes, delivery, destination, transportation and
incidental services; Section VII covers technical and quality requirements; and Section VIII covers qualification criteria.
nfilecitenturn6file2nL148-L205n
2. Clarifications
Bidders may submit written clarification requests through the mock procurement portal up to 23 September 2026, 17:00
hrs. DDLI may issue consolidated clarifications or corrigenda before the bid submission deadline.
3. Preparation of Bids
(cid:127) The bidder shall submit one complete techno-commercial bid and one financial BOQ.
(cid:127) All uploaded documents shall be legible and signed where required.
(cid:127) Scanned copies shall be self-attested where the tender requires self-attestation.
(cid:127) Technical deviations shall be clearly listed in Form 3 and commercial deviations in Form 5.
(cid:127) Conditional offers may be treated as non-responsive where the condition affects a material requirement.
4. Bid Validity
The bid shall remain valid for 120 days from the date of opening of the techno-commercial bid. DDLI may request an
extension in writing where permitted.
5. Evaluation
Evaluation will proceed in stages: preliminary scrutiny, eligibility and documentary checks, qualification assessment,
technical compliance, commercial/terms compliance, and financial evaluation among responsive bidders. The lowest
evaluated responsive offer will be considered in accordance with the stated evaluation conditions and applicable
preferences.

Section IV: General Conditions of Contract (GCC)
1. Contract Documents and Precedence
The contract shall comprise the Letter of Award, accepted bid, Tender Document, Schedule of Requirements, Technical
Specifications, SCC, agreed clarifications/corrigenda and other documents expressly incorporated into the contract. In
case of conflict, the order of precedence stated in the contract shall apply.
2. Supplier Obligations
(cid:127) Maintain eligibility and qualification during contract execution.
(cid:127) Supply new, unused and genuine goods meeting the specified technical requirements.
(cid:127) Provide all accessories, cables, adapters and documentation necessary for normal operation.
(cid:127) Complete installation/configuration and handover at the consignee location.
(cid:127) Provide warranty support for the complete warranty period.
(cid:127) Protect confidential information received during contract performance.
3. Inspection and Quality Assurance
DDLI or its nominated inspection representative may inspect and test goods before dispatch and/or after delivery. Initial
inspection or acceptance shall not remove the consignee's right to reject goods later found not to conform to the contract.
The uploaded MTD specifically provides for inspection before dispatch and retains the consignee's right to reject goods
later found deficient against technical specifications and quality requirements. nfilecitenturn5file8nL565-L605n
4. Packing and Transportation
Goods shall be securely packed in manufacturer-standard protective packaging suitable for road transportation and
handling. The supplier shall bear transportation and transit risk until delivery at the stated destination.
5. Delivery Delays
Time is of the essence. Delays not covered by approved extension provisions may attract liquidated damages at 0.5% of
the value of delayed goods per completed week, subject to a maximum of 5% of the delayed portion, without prejudice to
other contractual remedies.
DDLI/PROC/GOODS/2026-27/014 | FICTIONAL TRAINING DOCUMENT Page 7

Section IV: GCC – Prices, Payments, Warranty and Disputes
6. Prices and Taxes
Quoted prices shall be firm and inclusive of packing, forwarding, freight, insurance, installation, configuration and
incidental services up to the consignee location. GST and other statutory taxes shall be shown separately in the financial
BOQ.
7. Payment
Payment shall normally be made within 30 days of successful delivery, installation, acceptance and submission of an
undisputed invoice with required supporting documents. No advance payment is applicable.
8. Warranty
The supplier shall provide a minimum three-year comprehensive onsite warranty from the date of acceptance. Warranty
service shall include repair or replacement of defective components and reasonable technical support without additional
charge.
9. Performance Security
The successful bidder shall furnish performance security equal to 3% of the accepted contract value in the prescribed
form within the period stated in the Letter of Award.
10. Dispute Resolution
The parties shall first attempt resolution through the designated procurement officers. Unresolved disputes may be
referred to the arbitration mechanism stated in the contract, with the seat of arbitration in New Delhi and proceedings
governed by applicable Indian law.
11. Termination
The procuring entity may terminate the contract for material breach, persistent delay, insolvency or other grounds
specified in the contract, subject to applicable contractual procedure.
12. Code of Integrity
Bidders and the supplier shall not engage in bribery, collusion, coercion, fraudulent practice, conflict-of-interest
concealment or other prohibited conduct in connection with the tender or contract.
DDLI/PROC/GOODS/2026-27/014 | FICTIONAL TRAINING DOCUMENT Page 8

(cid:127) Manufacturer/OEM serial numbers shall be traceable to the supplied units.
(cid:127) Software licenses shall be genuine and correspond to the supplied devices.
(cid:127) Technical datasheets submitted with the bid shall identify the proposed make/model.
(cid:127) DDLI may verify key parameters against manufacturer documentation.
(cid:127) Any discrepancy between the quoted model and supplied model may be treated as a material deviation.
2. Pre-dispatch Inspection
DDLI may inspect a representative sample at the supplier's premises before dispatch. The supplier shall provide access
to the offered model, serial-number information and relevant manufacturer documentation.
3. Delivery Acceptance
Final acceptance will be based on quantity, physical condition, serial-number verification, technical conformity,
installation/configuration and satisfactory demonstration of the specified operating environment.
